principles: Only source-grounded traditional significations and strength/placement rules may be mapped to behavioral domains.
No V1.1/V1.2 owner-specific feature weights or owner-case ranks are supplied.
If a behavioral domain lacks a clear source-supported traditional analogue, abstain rather than invent one.

summary: Mercury: education, letters, disputation, reasoning, interpretation, accounts, communication, discoveries, forethought and intelligence, oratory, philosophy, systematic work.
Jupiter: political ties, friendships, justice, offices, rank, authority, beneficence, fellowship, relief from troubles, freedom.
Mars: action and effort, conflict, force, quarrels, difficult embassies, craftwork.
Venus: desire and love, friendship, companionship, agreements, pleasure, arts, beauty, marriage.
Saturn: necessity, isolation/solitariness, obstacles, secrets, griefs, confinement.
Valens states that appropriately/favorably situated benefics, and even malefics in appropriate places and their own sect, can manifest their proper effects.
Solar/day sect includes Sun, Jupiter and Saturn; lunar/night sect includes Moon, Venus and Mars.
Sect appropriateness is treated as a condition affecting whether a planet's proper effects operate constructively.
Mercury is associated with speech, memory, reasoning, learning, oratory and practical intelligence.
Jupiter with justice, counsel, religion, scholarship and public responsibility.
Sun with honour, authority and public office.
Venus with love, pleasure, art and sociability.
Mars with action, conflict, technical/craft activity and force.
Saturn with solitude, restraint, difficulty and endurance.
Moon with movement, messaging, care/nurture and the common people.
1st: life/self/body.
2nd: wealth/resources.
3rd: siblings, neighbours, short travel, letters/messages.
4th: home/land/family roots/endings.
5th: children, pleasure, play.
6th: illness, service, labour/workers.
7th: marriage/partners, open conflict/opponents.
8th: death/inheritance/fear/anguish.
9th: religion, learning, books, dreams/visions, long journeys.
10th: profession, office, honour, authority.
11th: friends, hope, trust, allies/councillors.
12th: sorrow, confinement, hidden enemies, self-undoing.
Lilly publishes an explicit strength/debility point table including essential dignity, house placement, motion, speed, solar phase and other conditions.
This project may use the published point table only as a source-native sensitivity arm; it must not alter Lilly's point values.

Phaladeepika gives explicit positional/planetary strength rules including exaltation, own/friendly signs, kendra/other bhava placement, directional strength, waxing/waning Moon, retrograde strength and other conditions.
A planet's strength can be assessed from multiple traditional testimonies rather than a project-authored salience coefficient.
Bhava judgement combines the bhava itself, its lord and its karaka/significator.
The text treats strength of the bhava, its lord and karaka as relevant to whether the bhava produces its effects.
Examples identify the 4th with mother/home, 5th with children, 7th with spouse, 10th with profession/activity, and 2nd with wealth/speech.
Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra has dedicated chapters for planetary characters, zodiacal signs, house effects, bhava lords, planetary aspects, strength evaluation and planetary karakatwas.
Planetary aspects include special aspect rules for Saturn, Mars and Jupiter.
Traditional planetary joys: Mercury 1st, Moon 3rd, Venus 5th, Mars 6th, Sun 9th, Jupiter 11th, Saturn 12th.
Joy is treated as a traditional positive testimony distinct from essential dignity.
William Lilly used the Regiomontanus house system; V1.3 Lilly specifications therefore use Regiomontanus cusps.

Lahiri ayanamsha was introduced by the Indian Calendar Reform Committee and became a standard basis for Indian sidereal ephemerides/calendars; V1.3 freezes Swiss Ephemeris Lahiri for its Parashari arm.

domain_ontology.definition: tendency to organize, parse or make sense of complex or conflicting structure/detail
persistent return to unresolved, hidden, existential or difficult questions
creating or originating one's own methods, ideas or contributions rather than only following inherited ones
expressing, explaining or translating understanding so other people can use it
trying to influence, argue, negotiate or persuade in a context-sensitive way
entry into roles/opportunities through recognition, invitation, appointment or acknowledged competence
opportunities and work emerging through friends, allies, communities or social connections
other people placing expectations, dependency, leadership or rescue roles onto the person
rapid embodied, intuitive or pre-deliberative signals used in decisions
self-direction, personal agency and preference for choosing one's own direction
importance of home, physical comfort, environmental conditions or a restorative private base
romantic attraction, affection, sensuality, sexuality and pair-bonding
emotional responsiveness, receptivity or susceptibility to other people's emotional states
capacity and limits for sustained work, labour or productive effort
mobilizing effort for work or causes judged meaningful or consequential
noticing and correcting errors, problems or disorder when they matter enough
withdrawal, privacy, solitude, spiritual retreat or removal from ordinary social activity
durable moral/value conflicts, competing obligations or tensions between principles
motives around money, property, resources, security, autonomy or status
